title: diranersen
summary: AD is a neurodegenerative disease with symptoms of progressive loss of memory and cognitive function. An intriguing approach to treat AD involves tau level reduction via ASOs (antisense oligonucleotides). Biogen and Ionis Pharmaceuticals co-developed diranersen, which targets and silences the pre-mRNA from the MAPT gene that encodes tau. Diranersen reduced total tau levels, but the clinical trial missed its primary endpoint of demonstrating dose-dependency for cognitive decline. These results raise questions about the relationship between tau level reduction and clinical efficacy in AD.

title: TNG456
summary: Tango Therapeutics has advanced TNG456, its third oral, MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor, into clinical trials. Derived from the same oxamide scaffold as Tango’s earlier candidates TNG908 and vopimetostat (TNG462), TNG456 combines improved potency and selectivity for MTAP-deleted cells with good CNS exposure across preclinical species. The latter property is particularly notable because MTAP deletions occur in over 40% of high-grade malignant gliomas. Tango dosed the first patient in a Ph. 1/2 trial in May 2025 and published the molecule’s discovery story in May 2026.
